questions.prompt: Match each mirror to its use.
questions.explain: Concave mirrors focus light and magnify close objects; convex mirrors give a wide view.

questions.prompt: What kind of image does a convex mirror ALWAYS form?
questions.explain: Convex mirrors spread light out, so the image is always virtual, upright and smaller.

questions.prompt: In the Optics Bench, a candle is placed very close to a concave mirror (between the pole and F). The image is…
questions.explain: This is how shaving and make-up mirrors work.

questions.prompt: A candle is placed at C (centre of curvature) of a concave mirror. The image is…
options: at C, real, inverted and the same size
questions.explain: At C the image forms at C too, inverted and the same size.

questions.prompt: Why are the bulbs of torches and headlights placed at the focus of a concave mirror?
options: So the reflected rays come out parallel as a strong beam
To make the image upside down
questions.explain: Light from the focus reflects parallel to the principal axis.

questions.prompt: Can a concave mirror form this image? (Think about where the object is.)
questions.explain: A single mirror's real images are always inverted, so ‘upright and real’ is impossible.

questions.prompt: Solar cookers often use a large concave mirror. Explain how it works, and discuss one benefit and one drawback of solar cookers for families in India.
questions.modelAnswer: The concave mirror reflects parallel rays of sunlight and concentrates them at its focus, where the cooking pot is placed, so the pot gets very hot. Benefit: free, clean energy with no smoke, saving money on LPG or firewood and reducing indoor air pollution. Drawbacks: it only works on sunny days and during daytime, cooking is slow, and it must be turned to follow the Sun.
rubric: Concave mirror concentrates sunlight at the focus
A valid benefit (free, clean, no smoke)
questions.explain: Criterion D: connect optics to energy and daily life.

questions.text: A mirror that curves inwards like the inside of a spoon is ___. A mirror that bulges outwards is ___.
questions.explain: Concave caves in; convex bulges out.
